dva-avc-063.text: A team configures a function AWS Lambda to execute within a VPC (in private subnets), so that it can connect to a database Amazon RDS The team heard that functions Lambda connected to one VPC historically suffered significant additional latency from cold start due to the creation/annexation of an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) by running environment, and is concerned about the impact of this on latency of the function.

dva-avc-064.text: Multiple functions AWS Lambda can compete to create a 'lock' object (e.g. 'locks/job')-123.lock') no Amazon S3 to claim exclusive processing rights of a job. 'If-None-Match: *' does the S3 perform the existence verification and the ATOMIC write on the server side: if another invocation has already created the lock object, the request fails with 412, ensuring that only PRIMEIRA Invocation to arrive creates the object successfully — without a running condition window between verification and writing.
dva-avc-064.hint: Think of which conditional header of the S3, introduced to 'PutObject', allows the writing to occur only if the key does not yet exist, atomically.

Incorrect. This is a classic 'verify-after-write' pattern vulnerable to running condition: two competing invocations can both call 'HeadObject', both receive 404, and both continue to 'PutObject', both believing they have acquired the lock.

Incorrect. Without conditional headers, 'CopyObject' has the same standard behavior as 'PutObject' — overwrites an existing destination object — not providing any additional semantics of 'Only the first writer wins' beyond 'PutObject' (with or without conditionals) already offers.

Incorrect. dva-avc-069.text: A function AWS Lambda is invoked asynchronously (activated by notifications of events of the Amazon S3) to send time-sensitive push notifications, such as 'your race is coming now'.
